title: The Oldest Game: An LLM-powered word duel (Demo)
author: whoji
selftext:
Sharing a little demo I made: The Oldest Game 

[https://oldest.tier9.games](https://oldest.tier9.games)



It's inspired by ["The Oldest Game" in The Sandman](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iZOwaeAEIw0&t), the duel where Dream and Lucifer fight with nothing but words: "I am a wolf." "I am a hunter."  ... until one of them says "I am hope." (It was Dream vs Choronzon form the book but Netflix did a great job adapting the scene). I've loved Neil Gaiman's fictions for a long time, and that scene stuck with me.

How it plays: each turn you write one sentence, anything at all.  e.g. Morpheus in his dreamy voice: "I am a spider, fly-consuming, eight-legged." A frozen river cracks open and a kelpie climbs out." An AI /LLM Judge reads it and turns it into a TCG-style summons card with a cost, attack, defense, an element. Bigger ideas cost more, and if you overreach, the spell backfires on you. 

While building it I kept borrowing elements from early gen Pokemon and Bizzard's Hearthstone. And when I finally played it, it felt like none of those.  Bot like Sandman's The Oldest Game either. It felt more like[ Cardcaptor Sakura](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_uFwK4nacjI) = )

I had this idea for a long time but shelved it. Asking an LLM to judge every single sentence was too slow (seconds per turn) and too expensive to put in front of players. Then last month TypeSafe released Jev, a decision model that answers typed questions instead of writing text. It judges a sentence in about a quarter of a second, for a fraction of the cost. That made it possible, so I rebuilt the whole thing around it and turned it into this demo.

Let me know what you think.
